# Question and data

How do dry-weight measurements differ among the three groups in R's documented `PlantGrowth` dataset? The data contain 30 observations. Consult `?PlantGrowth` for provenance and units; the group labels do not justify assigning fertilizer names.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-summary
#| tbl-cap: "Observed group means and standard deviations."
data("PlantGrowth", package = "datasets")
summary_table <- PlantGrowth |>
  dplyr::group_by(group) |>
  dplyr::summarise(n = dplyr::n(), mean = mean(weight), sd = sd(weight), .groups = "drop")
knitr::kable(summary_table, digits = 2)
```

# Distribution and model

```{r}
#| label: fig-groups
#| fig-cap: "Dry-weight observations by documented treatment group."
boxplot(weight ~ group, data = PlantGrowth, xlab = "Group", ylab = "Dry weight")
stripchart(weight ~ group, data = PlantGrowth, vertical = TRUE,
           method = "jitter", add = TRUE, pch = 19, col = "#245A42")
fit <- aov(weight ~ group, data = PlantGrowth)
summary(fit)
TukeyHSD(fit)
```

# Diagnostics

```{r}
par(mfrow = c(1, 2))
plot(fit, which = 1)
plot(fit, which = 2)
```

# Interpretation

The observed mean for group trt2 is `r round(summary_table$mean[summary_table$group == "trt2"], 2)`. Discuss @tbl-summary and @fig-groups, the global F-test, one adjusted pairwise interval, residual behaviour, and the limits of the documented design. Replace this instruction with your own interpretation before submission.
